answer: Each identity must publish one unique dataset of at least 1000 distinct records, hashed on-chain, with a 20 POA deposit locked 60 days; any dataset over 80% similar to an existing one is rejected and its deposit slashed. A lantern over the registry exposes copies at once. Each extra fake needs a fresh dataset plus another 20 POA, so 100 fakes cost 100 datasets and 2,000 POA, and inventing data grows harder as the registry fills. The deposit is an anchor of honesty, and only datasets passing the summit of similarity audits unlock payouts, which verifiers check by recomputing hashes and scores.
